differences.how: T-3176: the 1911 sheet draws a square turned 45 degrees across the corner (2.27 m on a face, centred on u 23.98, v 15.55), the photograph a broad face about 3.2 m across (3.5 times the front's 1.15 m window beside it); re-solving the camera with the square's side free on the sheet's centre gives 3.25 m at 4.4 px RMS, where the sheet's 2.27 m leaves 40-47 px. Built as K08's polygonal tower turned 45 degrees across the front's south corner (centre 0.42 m inside the front, on the flank's plane), its north-west, south-west and south-east faces outside the walls, the storey bands at 7.5 and 12.6 m, its wall top 16.2 m, a hip at pitch 3.46 cut to a 1.0 m deck at 22.0 m, an iron crest 0.6 m tall round the deck and a finial on each of its corners; the render's tower edges stand within about 10 px of the print's

differences.what: the pavilion's steep pyramidal roof over the cornice, with its finial and its triple attic lights (x 330-560 px, y 350-830); the render showed the pavilion's low hip under the main mansard. T-3175 carries the pavilion up an attic storey from the main eave to its own cornice at the main curb's height (y about 605 px, 16.8 m), three tall lights in its wall, under a slated crown hipped on every side at 47 degrees to a point (about 20.5 m) and a turned iron finial
the rear part's step out on the south flank (the sheet's 1.6 m at u 0-14.6), seen past the corner at x 1080-1150 px
the carved hoods over the pavilion's lights and the segmental hoods over the window bay's (plain lintels stand in)
the alternating light and dark stone courses of the front and flank
the porch's round arches and its steps rising along the front from the north (a flight stands across the porch's width)
the barred basement lights' full height, about 1.5 m (K02's two base courses hold them to 0.75 m)
the window heights and places on the front and in the pavilion, read through the camera
differences.how: they render within about 0.3 m of the print's

differences.what: the stone's colour
differences.how: the print is monochrome; Lemont limestone is reconstructed (L-k01-1827-doane-3171)

differences.what: the north flank, the rear and the brick rear range
the pavilion's north edge (x 270 px) and its crown and attic, which T-3171's camera put 98 px and 60-90 px east of the print's
differences.how: T-3176's re-solved camera: the pavilion's edges are two of the plan readings it is fitted to, and render within about 10 px of the print's

differences.what: the crown's cornice stands 0.65 m past the pavilion's sides, the kit's least past the main cornice's 0.6 m, where the print's stands about at them (its eave x 350-597 px against the pavilion's face to x 600), and the attic's wall is stone across the pavilion's whole width, where the print slates its outer parts as cheeks (x 535-600 on its south side) and sets the lights between stone piers
the attic's three lights: the print's carry arched transom heads under carved hoods (y about 627-690 px); the build's flat transoms stand in
the crown's pitch: the print's rise of about 3.4 m over a half-width of about 3.4 m reads 45 degrees, the build's 47 (the kit's steep range starts over 45), its point about 0.3 m higher
the crown's finial: the print's is a wrought iron cross-like finial about 1 m tall (y 355-410 px); the build turns the deck's iron finial (T-3000) to the same height

the heights: through the re-solved camera, read with the sheet's widths, the print puts the water table at about 1.2 m, the string course at 5.2 m and the main cornice's top at 9.4 m over grade, where the record has 2.0, 7.5 and 12.6 m (read through T-3171's camera, which stood on an assumed corner point); the render's house and tower stand about a third taller than the print's, the main cornice at about y 580 against the print's 800 px. The tower's own heights are read from the print in proportion to the main cornice there (its wall top 1.29 times it, its deck 1.75), so they come down with the house's
the tower's cornice: the print's deep moulded cornice over a row of brackets (y 485-525 px); the build's plain soffit and fascia 0.45 m out stand in
the tower's lights: the print's carry segmental hoods over the principal floor's pair and a roundel between the second floor's (y 1130-1160 px); the build's flat stone heads stand in
the tower's slated hip: the print's flares a little at its foot (a bellcast about 0.2 m out over the bottom metre); the build's runs straight at one pitch

the deck's crest: the print's band is pierced by four round holes a face and carries two finials (crossed iron tops) on its near corners; the build's band is solid, and carries a turned finial on each of its four corners, the far two standing behind the near two from this camera
the tower's south-east face: not seen; built with the south-west face's paired lights (L-k01-1827-doane-3171)
